subject: Reconcile: microfloor mapping and concession language for BrightCart
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@brightcart.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightCart Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Question on how leftover credits map to long-history sessions

Hi Logan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked for one more clarification before we sign the SOW: how do leftover token credits apply when a single user session has >24k tokens (we expect a small % of search+history flows to hit that)? Specifically:

- Do we get fractional credits refunded or rounded up to the next minimum?
- How are "microfloors" applied across interleaved sessions (same user using search and chat in parallel)?

Attached is the draft SOW procurement pulled together. If you can send a short example invoice line (or spreadsheet) that maps a few scenarios to the proposed concession language, that'd be ideal.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Jenkins
Head of Integrations, BrightCart

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Question on how leftover credits map to long-history sessions

On Wed, Jul 11, 2028 at 09:12 Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sarah —
>
> Quick note to acknowledge receipt. We're aligning a short worked example and a recommended concession clause. Marissa: can you validate the invoice examples (low/medium/high history cases)? Ben: can you confirm whether the pilot concession we discussed (50% credit against microfloor for first 3 months) is still ok from our side?

Attached is the spreadsheet with three scenarios (rows):
- Scenario A: short session (<=4k tokens) — billed normally, no microfloor hit.
- Scenario B: medium history (8k-20k tokens) — microfloor rounds up to nearest 1,000 token quantum; show partial credit calculation.
- Scenario C: long-history (24k-36k tokens) — split across conversation buckets: first 16k billed at session quantum, excess billed as "overlength" with amortized microfloor in month.

Key recommendation in the SOW language:
- Explicit mapping: "Excess tokens beyond the model's standard session cap will be billed as overlength tokens with a prorated microfloor application; partial-token credits will be represented as invoice line adjustments and not as fractional refunds."
- Pilot concession (approved by finance for SR demo accounts): 50% microfloor credit for the first 3 months for accounts migrating from legacy providers; accrues monthly and appears as a negative invoice line.

Tessa, flagged a couple of places in the SOW where legal wants clearer fallback language (see comments).

Marissa
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: billing-examples.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on how leftover credits map to long-history sessions

Logan / Marissa —

Confirming finance sign-off on the concession for this one-off pilot:
- 50% credit against the monthly microfloor for months 1-3 (applies to invoice month-end as a credit line).
- No cumulative refunds — credits are non-cash and cannot be carried back beyond the 3-month window.
- For long-history sessions, we'll apply amortized billing: split the session into active buckets (full microfloor units) and an overlength bucket that is billed per-token with rounding to the token quantum; if the overlength bucket falls below the microfloor, apply the 50% credit to that bucket for the pilot period.

We'll need procurement to accept an invoice sample that states "credits applied as negative invoice lines; no cash refunds" and to initial the SOW amendment.

Ben
Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@brightcart.com>, BrightCart Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jul 2028 17:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on how leftover credits map to long-history sessions

Sarah —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is the SOW excerpt we propose (highlighted) plus the worked invoice examples that map three real usage snapshots to invoice lines. Short summary:

- Rounding: tokens are rounded up to the nearest 1,000-token quantum for microfloor evaluation; billing per-token still applies to overlength buckets after quantum bucketing.
- Partial credits: we do not issue cash refunds; partial credits show as a negative invoice line applied within the billing month.
- Pilot concession: 50% credit to the microfloor for months 1–3; credits unapplied after the window do not carry forward.

Action items for BrightCart:
1) Please confirm you accept the "credits as negative invoice lines" wording (we've added the sentence procurement requested).
2) If ok, could procurement initial the highlighted amendment on page 2 of the SOW PDF and upload to the DocuSign link? (link included below).

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/BRG-3921/sow
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/BRG-3921

If procurement prefers a different credit presentation, loop Ben and Tessa — we can adapt invoice formatting but not change the concession window.

Best,
Logan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
